item: Row 446 P1: the re-index drain holds the writer up to 30 s while nothing else writes
summary: While the collector is stopped and no import window is open (the backlog drain's idle branch), and while an import owns the machine (the restore's inline re-index), a re-index batch now commits at 500 articles (the precompute window) or 30 s of held gate instead of 200 articles or 10 s. The condition is re-read at every flush question, so the batch falls back to 10 s the moment the collector starts or the window ends; a queued writer (a UI save, the collector) still ends the batch after 1 s. OO_REINDEX_OWNED_HOLD_TARGET_S may lower the target, never raise it past 30 s; an explicit OO_REINDEX_HOLD_TARGET_S or OO_IMPORT_REINDEX_COMMIT_BATCH is the operator's word and applies here too. Measured on a 150k encrypted store, 8,000 articles: commit 232.5 to 119.7 s (-49 %), writer 541 to 508 s, longest hold 38.2 s (watchdog 60 s). Each batch is still one transaction; no schema, version or durability change.
